cohort: The study included 392 mother-infant pairs delivered between April 2020 and July 2021 at a community hospital network in northeastern Pennsylvania, USA, with 198 mothers having confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection during pregnancy and 194 without.
finding: While SARS-CoV-2 infection during pregnancy was associated with increased maternal comorbidities and adverse birth outcomes, no significant disparities in neonatal developmental milestones or growth outcomes were observed up to 12 months of age.
mod_finding: Pregnant women with SARS-CoV-2 infection exhibited higher occurrences of cesarean section (CS) rates.
followup_time: 18 months (for ASQ scores), 12 months (for developmental milestones)
